topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Locality Principle
explanation: The memory hierarchy structures storage into levels of increasing latency and capacity, mitigating the performance disparity between the CPU and main memory (DRAM). Effective caching strategies fundamentally rely on the principle of locality. Temporal locality dictates that recently accessed data blocks will likely be accessed again soon, while spatial locality suggests that data near a recently accessed address will also be needed. By placing these frequently referenced blocks into faster cache levels (L1, L2, L3), the system exploits these principles. This exploitation significantly increases the cache hit rate, thereby reducing the average memory access time and maximizing system throughput.
